sourceFingerprint.method: SHA-256 of UTF-8 path + space + file SHA-256 lines; POSIX relative paths sorted by casefold(), joined with LF and no trailing LF.
documentationLimits: Source extraction and documentation do not supply an external quality ceiling: the committed code-led build has no approved comp or QUALITY BAR board.
The replacement verdict resolves only the two material fixes from the original full review.
Component snippets preserve CSS appearance and states. React/Leaflet data, persistence and native-dialog focus management remain in application source.
The eight visual captures are full-page images; viewport and PNG image dimensions are recorded separately.
Synthesized OKLCH ramps are panel metadata only. Hex frontmatter values remain normative; no generated ramp has been promoted to the application palette.
Coordinates, gauge datum, observations and geography are synthetic; this record does not establish forecast accuracy or physical-phone testing.

components.css: .ds-gauge-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 12px; background: var(--raised, #f6f8f8); border-radius: 6px; font-family: var(--font, 'Manrope Variable', 'Manrope', sans-serif); color: var(--text, #21343d); } .ds-gauge { display: flex; height: 68px; gap: 6px; align-items: stretch; } .ds-gauge-column { width: 17px; position: relative; background: #dde8e9; border-radius: 2px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-gauge-water { position: absolute; bottom: 0; left: 0; right: 0; background: var(--accent, #087f82); opacity: .75; } .ds-gauge-stale .ds-gauge-water { background: #81969e; } .ds-gauge-marks { display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1; color: var(--muted, #586a73); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-gauge-label { color: var(--muted, #586a73); font-size: 13px; } .ds-gauge-reading strong { display: block; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.4; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-gauge-reading small { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted, #586a73); } .ds-gauge-reading p { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #586a73); line-height: 1.45; margin: 3px 0 0; } .ds-validity { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; margin-top: 13px; font-family: var(--font, 'Manrope Variable', 'Manrope', sans-serif); font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #586a73); } .ds-reasons { margin-top: 8px; font-family: var(--font, 'Manrope Variable', 'Manrope', sans-serif); font-size: 13px; color: var(--text, #21343d); } .ds-reasons summary { cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; padding: 5px 0; } .ds-reasons summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #087f82); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-reasons p { margin: 6px 0; color: var(--muted, #586a73); } @media (max-width: 480px) { .ds-reasons { margin-top: 12px; } .ds-reasons summary { min-height: 40px; padding: 10px 0; } }

narrative.overview:
Floodline is a calm, precise information sheet for reading environmental evidence in daylight. A pale water-grey frame holds a white work surface. Manrope gives headings, ordinary web controls and measured figures one consistent voice. Compact labels, comparable rows and modest corners keep the map and its evidence easy to scan.

Depth comes from tone and hairline boundaries. Environmental data carries teal; amber and red describe warning and failure states. Missing evidence has its own words and patterned geometry. The gauge and observation, issue and validity times make the age and meaning of a reading visible alongside its value. These are durable visual commitments drawn from the implementation and the confirmed direction; the synthetic pilot is always labelled.
keyCharacteristics: Water-grey frame, white sheet and flat bordered panels.
Locally bundled Manrope with compact sentence-case labels and tabular figures.
Teal environmental evidence with separate amber, red and neutral state signals.
Patterned unknown areas, plain-language limitations and visible freshness.
Familiar navigation, keyboard focus and responsive resident forms.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Keep ordinary navigation and controls neutral. Use teal for environmental data and amber/red/green for their documented state meanings; the map's geographic and severity colors retain their distinct roles.

rules.name: The Unknown Rule
rules.body: Missing or stale evidence stays visibly unknown. Use the neutral tag and hatched cell; show "Unavailable" or "Not estimable" where a current value cannot be supported.

rules.name: The Comparable Figures Rule
rules.body: Use tabular numerals for totals, timestamps, rainfall, the relative index and gauge marks. Keep the unit and observation context visible with the number.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Keep the frame, work sheet and ordinary panels free of shadows. Preserve the small tooltip shadow and modal depth when those temporary layers are present.

dos: Do reuse the water-grey frame, white work sheet and flat panel hierarchy.
Do keep Manrope, sentence-case labels and tabular figures consistent across screens.
Do attach units, observation times, source meaning and validity to environmental values.
Do show Unknown with both a word and patterned geography, and keep stale readings visibly retained.
Do provide labelled controls, keyboard focus and a text route through map evidence.
Do preserve the shared gutters and verify resident flows at 1024px, 390px and 320px.
Do use the dedicated warning, failure and lifecycle states after the relevant action or evidence confirms them.
donts: Don't turn missing or stale observations into zero rainfall, an all-clear result or a current estimate.
Don't give the frame, sheet or ordinary dashboard panels decorative shadows.
Don't use teal to imply that an observation is verified, or a risk fill to imply a road is closed.
Don't hide risk, freshness or submission state behind color alone.
Don't display a saved-state confirmation before the submission succeeds.
Don't expand the relative demo index into an asserted flood probability or unlabeled live forecast.
Don't replace standard screen navigation with gestures or map-only interaction.
